Calculation of power per unit volume

All three reactors were mixed at the same power input per unit volume of mixed liquid condition (i.e., 5 W/m3). The gas flow rate for R-a and R-b and the impeller speed for R-m were calculated using Eqs. (1) and (2), respectively (Casey, 1986).

In Eq. (1), P is the power (W), V is the volume of the slurry mixed (m3), Gr is the air or biogas flow rate (m3/s/m3), P2 is the head space pressure (101,416.83 N/m2), P1 is the pressure at the injection point (i.e., P2 plus static head of slurry), and λ is 1.01 at 35 oC.

The pH and ORP were monitored online by pH and ORP probes (InPro 325X probe, M300 controller, Mettler Toledo, Urdof, Switzerland). Dissolved oxygen was measured using an oxygen probe (InPro 6800, Mettler Toledo,Urdof, Switzerland) The H2 concentration in the skin flap tissue was measured using a H2 sensor (Unisense, Denmark). TS and VS were measured over time in duplicate samples and were analyzed according to APHA standard methods (Association). VFAs (acetic, propionic and butyric acids) were assayed using an Agilent 7820A gas chromatograph (Agilent Technologies Inc., Santa Clara, CA, USA) coupled with a flame ionization detector (FID). The injector, oven and detector temperatures were 230, 220 and 240 oC, respectively. Nitrogen was used as the carrier gas (flow rate 50 mL/min). Samples and standards were acidified by the addition of 20 µL of H2SO4 (96–97% (w/v)) to each 1 mL sample before VFA analysis. A sample volume of 1 µL was injected. The sum of measured acetic, propionic and butyric acids was the total amount of VFA. The biogas produced in the bioreactors was collected in gas-tight bags. Biogas composition was determined using a gas chromatograph (GC) (SP-2100, Beijing Beifen-Ruili Analytical Instrument Co., Ltd., China) equipped with a thermal conductivity detector (TCD) and a packed Porapak Q column (3 m × 3 mm). Helium gas was used as the carrier gas (flow rate 10 mL/min). The temperatures of the inlet, the oven and the TCD were 100, 100 and 55 oC, respectively. The crude protein, crude fiber and crude fat contents were determined according to the standard method prescribed by the Chinese National Standards (GB/T6432-1994, GB/T6434-2006 and GB/T6433-2006)(Wang et al., 2018). Carbohydrate was calculated by subtracting the amount of crude fat, crude protein and crude fiber from the amount of VS.

At the conclusion of the experiment, sludge samples were collected from each reactor. Total genomic DNA was extracted using a PowerSoil DNA Isolation Kit (MO BIO, Carlsbad, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The extracted DNA concentrations of all samples were measured using a NanoDrop 2000 Spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA), and the DNA was stored at −20  °C until use.

To investigate the changes in bacterial and archaeal communities, the V3–V4 region of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene was amplified using the primers 338F (5′-ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG-3′) and 806R (5′-GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT-3′). The V3–V5 region of the archaeal 16S rRNA gene was amplified using the primers Arch344F (5′-ACGGGGYGCAGCAGGCGCGA-3′) and Arch915R (5′-GTGCTCCCCCGCCAATTCCT-3′). The DNA sequence was analyzed using an Illumina® MiSeq PE300 platform at Majorbio Bio-Pharm Technology Co., Ltd. (Shanghai, China). The optimized sequences were clustered into operational taxonomic units with a 97% similarity cut-off using the Usearch algorithm (version 7.1, http://drive5.com/uparse/). In addition, the Chao estimator was used to indicate the community richness and the Shannon and Simpson indexes were used to represent the community diversity.
